terms.definition: The practice of defining and managing cloud infrastructure using code files instead of manual console actions. Enables repeatability, consistency, and version control of infrastructure.
terms.example: Writing a YAML file that creates an EC2 instance and S3 bucket, then running it to create those resources automatically.

terms.definition: AWS's native, free IaC service. Uses YAML or JSON templates to define and deploy AWS resources as stacks. Cloud-specific — works only with AWS.
terms.example: Creating a template that provisions a VPC, EC2 instance, and RDS database, then deploying it as a stack named 'production-env'.

terms.definition: The YAML or JSON blueprint file you write for CloudFormation. Describes what AWS resources you want to create and how they should be configured.
terms.example: A .yaml file with a Resources section defining an EC2 instance with instance type t3.micro and a specific AMI ID.

terms.definition: The actual collection of AWS resources created and managed by a CloudFormation template. Resources in a stack are created, updated, and deleted together.
terms.example: After deploying your template, the stack 'my-app-stack' contains the EC2 instance, S3 bucket, and IAM role defined in the template.

terms.definition: Optional template section that accepts input values at stack creation time. Makes templates flexible and reusable across environments without editing the template itself.
terms.example: A parameter 'InstanceType' with a default of t3.micro allows you to pass t3.large for production without changing the template.

terms.definition: Optional template section that defines static lookup tables. Commonly used to map AWS regions to region-specific values like AMI IDs.
terms.example: A RegionMap that returns 'ami-abc123' for us-east-1 and 'ami-xyz789' for ap-south-1, looked up automatically with !FindInMap.

terms.definition: Optional template section that declares values to be displayed after stack creation. Also enables cross-stack references between separate stacks.
terms.example: An output that displays the public IP address of the created EC2 instance in the stack's Outputs tab.

terms.definition: An IaC approach where you describe your desired final state without specifying step-by-step how to achieve it. The IaC tool figures out the implementation.
terms.example: CloudFormation and Terraform are declarative — you say 'I want an EC2 with t3.micro' and the tool handles creation details.

terms.definition: An IaC approach where you write exact step-by-step instructions in a specific order. You control every action taken.
terms.example: Ansible playbooks listing tasks: first install nginx, then copy config file, then restart service — each step explicitly ordered.

terms.definition: Open-source, multi-cloud IaC tool by HashiCorp. Uses HCL (HashiCorp Configuration Language). Works with AWS, Azure, GCP, and 1000+ providers.
terms.example: Writing a main.tf file that creates resources in both AWS and Azure in a single apply.

terms.definition: The configuration language used by Terraform to define infrastructure. Human-readable and declarative.
terms.example: resource "aws_instance" "web" { ami = "ami-abc" instance_type = "t3.micro" }

terms.definition: Open-source, agentless, push-based configuration management tool. Manages software inside servers — installs packages, updates config files, manages services — using SSH.
terms.example: An Ansible playbook that installs nginx on 50 servers simultaneously by pushing the task from the control node.

terms.definition: A configuration management approach where target servers do not need any special management software installed. The control node handles all communication.
terms.example: Ansible is agentless — only the master server needs Ansible. Target EC2 instances need nothing installed besides SSH access.

terms.definition: Configuration management model where the master/control node actively sends commands to target servers. Opposite of pull-based.
terms.example: Ansible pushes playbook tasks to all target servers over SSH when you run 'ansible-playbook site.yml'.

terms.definition: Configuration management model where target servers periodically contact the master server to fetch and apply configuration updates.
terms.example: Chef and Puppet require agents on each server that pull configuration from the Chef/Puppet master every N minutes.

terms.definition: Software pre-installed on Amazon Linux 2, Amazon Linux 2023, and AWS Windows AMIs. Runs on EC2 instances and communicates with AWS Systems Manager to enable all SSM features.
terms.example: The SSM Agent running on an EC2 instance allows Session Manager to connect without SSH and Patch Manager to apply updates.

terms.definition: AWS Systems Manager sub-service that provides browser-based shell or CLI access to EC2 instances without SSH keys, open ports, or bastion hosts.
terms.example: Connecting to a private EC2 instance in a subnet with no public IP by clicking 'Start Session' in the SSM console.

terms.definition: AWS Systems Manager sub-service that executes shell commands or scripts on one or many managed instances simultaneously, without SSH.
terms.example: Running 'sudo yum update -y' on all 100 EC2 instances tagged 'Environment: production' with a single Run Command invocation.

terms.definition: AWS Systems Manager sub-service that automates security patching of managed instances on a defined schedule using patch baselines and maintenance windows.
terms.example: Scheduling weekly patch scans and installations every Sunday at 2 AM for all production instances using a maintenance window.

terms.definition: AWS Systems Manager sub-service providing secure, hierarchical storage for configuration data and secrets. SecureString type uses KMS encryption.
terms.example: Storing a database password as /myapp/prod/db-password of type SecureString, retrieved by EC2 at runtime via the AWS SDK.

terms.definition: Any EC2 instance (or on-premises server) that has the SSM Agent installed, running, and correctly configured with an IAM role. Appears in Fleet Manager.
terms.example: An EC2 instance with AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore role attached and SSM Agent running shows up as a managed node in Fleet Manager.

terms.definition: AWS Systems Manager capability that shows a centralized dashboard of all managed nodes — their status, software inventory, and system details.
terms.example: Viewing all 50 EC2 instances across your account in Fleet Manager to see which have the SSM Agent online.

terms.definition: AWS managed IAM policy that grants the minimum permissions needed for Systems Manager to manage an EC2 instance. Should be attached to the instance's IAM role.
terms.example: Creating an IAM role with AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore and attaching it to an EC2 instance so SSM Agent can communicate with Systems Manager.

terms.definition: A preview of what will change in a CloudFormation stack before you apply an update. Shows resources that will be Added, Modified, or Replaced.
terms.example: Creating a Change Set before updating a stack to see that your change will Replace (delete and recreate) the EC2 instance before committing.

terms.definition: Visual drag-and-drop builder built into AWS CloudFormation that auto-generates YAML/JSON templates from resources you place on a canvas.
terms.example: Dragging EC2 and S3 icons onto the composer canvas and clicking 'Template' tab to see the auto-generated YAML.
